findings.title: Server-Side JavaScript injection via eval() of contribution inputs
findings.attack_path: Authenticated user submits preTax/afterTax/roth on POST /contributions. Each value is passed straight to eval() before numeric validation, so a payload such as 'res.end(require("child_process").execSync("id"))' or a long-running loop runs in the Node process. This yields arbitrary code execution on the application server and a pivot to the MongoDB tier.
findings.remediation: Replace eval() with parseInt(req.body.x, 10)/Number() and reject NaN; never evaluate user input as code. Run the process with least privilege.

findings.title: NoSQL injection via unsanitized $where in allocations threshold
findings.attack_path: GET /allocations/:userId?threshold= passes threshold unescaped into a MongoDB $where JavaScript string: this.stocks > '<threshold>'. An attacker supplies 0';while(true){}' to hang the server, or 1'; return 1 == '1 to bypass the filter and read all users' allocations. $where executes server-side JS in the database engine.
findings.remediation: Drop $where; use a typed comparison query with parseInt-validated numeric bounds (0..99), reject otherwise. Disable server-side JS in MongoDB (--noscripting).

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in research stock lookup
findings.attack_path: GET /research builds url = req.query.url + req.query.symbol and calls needle.get(url) server-side, echoing the response body to the client. An authenticated attacker sets url to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (cloud metadata) or an internal service to read credentials/internal endpoints and exfiltrate them through the rendered response.
findings.remediation: Remove caller-controlled URLs; use a fixed allowlisted upstream base, validate the symbol, block link-local/private/loopback ranges, and disable response reflection.

findings.title: Plaintext password storage and plaintext credential comparison
findings.attack_path: addUser stores password as a raw string and validateLogin compares fromDB === fromUser. bcrypt-nodejs is imported but the hashing/compare lines are commented out. Any read of the users collection (via TM-002 NoSQL, a backup, or DB compromise) exposes every cleartext password, enabling account takeover and credential reuse across systems.
findings.remediation: Hash with bcrypt.hashSync(password, genSaltSync()) on signup and bcrypt.compareSync on login; migrate existing rows; never store or log cleartext passwords.

findings.title: Sensitive PII (SSN, DOB, bank account/routing) stored in cleartext
findings.attack_path: Profile updateUser writes ssn, dob, bankAcc, bankRouting directly to the users document with no encryption (the crypto encrypt/decrypt helpers are commented out). Any database read path (NoSQL injection, RCE, stolen backup) yields regulated financial PII in cleartext, a reportable breach.
findings.remediation: Encrypt SSN/DOB/bank fields at rest using a managed KMS-backed key; restrict field access; add field-level access logging.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on allocations userId
findings.attack_path: displayAllocations takes userId from the URL path param, not the session, and queries with no ownership check. An authenticated user iterates GET /allocations/1, /2, /3 to read any other user's allocations plus the joined userName/firstName/lastName, harvesting account data horizontally.
findings.remediation: Derive userId from req.session.userId; if path-param access is required, enforce an ownership/role check before querying.

findings.title: Stored XSS via memos and disabled template autoescaping
findings.attack_path: POST /memos stores memo text unsanitized; GET /memos renders every memo with marked() into a shared list seen by all users with swig autoescape:false. A crafted markdown/HTML payload executes script in every viewer's session, including any admin who opens /memos, enabling session-cookie theft (cookies lack httpOnly) and account takeover.
findings.remediation: Set swig autoescape:true, keep marked sanitize:true and add a server-side HTML sanitizer (DOMPurify), scope memos per user, and set httpOnly on the session cookie.

findings.title: Missing function-level access control on benefits admin endpoint
findings.attack_path: GET/POST /benefits are guarded only by isLoggedIn; the isAdmin middleware exists but is commented out in index.js. Any authenticated non-admin user lists all non-admin users and overwrites arbitrary users' benefitStartDate via POST /benefits, a vertical privilege/business-logic abuse.
findings.remediation: Add isAdmin to both /benefits routes; enforce role checks server-side on every privileged function.

findings.title: Hardcoded session secret and crypto keys in source
findings.attack_path: config/env/all.js commits cookieSecret 'session_cookie_secret_key_here' and cryptoKey 'a_secure_key_for_crypto_here'. With the signing secret known, an attacker forges/tampers session cookies to impersonate any user (set userId to an admin's id) and any data encrypted with the static cryptoKey is recoverable.
findings.remediation: Load secrets from environment/secret manager, generate a strong random session secret per deployment, rotate keys, and remove the values from source control history.

findings.title: Committed TLS private key and certificate in repository
findings.attack_path: artifacts/cert/server.key contains a BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY checked into the repo alongside server.crt. Anyone with repo access (or a leaked clone) can impersonate the TLS endpoint or decrypt captured TLS traffic if this key is ever used in a real deployment.
findings.remediation: Remove the private key from the repo and history, treat it as compromised, regenerate the keypair, and provision certs via a secret store / ACME at deploy time.

findings.title: Open redirect in /learn via unvalidated query URL
findings.attack_path: GET /learn does res.redirect(req.query.url) with no validation. An attacker crafts /learn?url=https://evil.example/phish and uses the trusted app domain to redirect victims to a phishing or malware page, lending credibility to credential-harvesting.
findings.remediation: Redirect only to a server-side allowlist of relative paths or known hosts; reject absolute external URLs.

findings.title: Session cookie missing httpOnly/secure and no fixation defense on login
findings.attack_path: express-session is configured without a cookie httpOnly/secure flag (commented out) and handleLoginRequest sets req.session.userId without req.session.regenerate(). A pre-set session id survives login (fixation), and any XSS (TM-007) can read document.cookie to hijack sessions; plaintext HTTP (TM-013) exposes the cookie on the wire.
findings.remediation: Set cookie { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }, regenerate the session on login, and use a generic cookie name.

findings.title: Application served over plaintext HTTP with security middleware disabled
findings.attack_path: server.js starts http.createServer (HTTPS block commented out) and all helmet protections (HSTS, frameguard, CSP, noSniff) and CSRF are disabled. Credentials, session cookies, SSN and bank data travel in cleartext, exposing them to network MITM, and the missing headers leave clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and CSRF unmitigated.
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS (or front with a TLS-terminating proxy), enable helmet (HSTS/CSP/frameguard/noSniff), enable csurf for state-changing routes.

findings.title: Reflected XSS on profile website field via wrong-context encoding
findings.attack_path: displayProfile HTML-encodes doc.website then renders it both as an input value and inside an href link with autoescape off. HTML encoding does not neutralize a javascript: URL or attribute-breaking payload in the link context, so a stored website value executes script when the profile is rendered.
findings.remediation: Encode per output context (URL-encode for href, scheme-allowlist http/https), enable swig autoescape, and validate the website field.

findings.title: Catastrophic-backtracking ReDoS in bank routing validation
findings.attack_path: handleProfileUpdate validates bankRouting with /([0-9]+)+#/ (nested quantifier). A POST /profile body such as a long run of digits with no trailing # forces exponential backtracking, pinning a CPU core and degrading or hanging the single-threaded Node event loop (DoS).
findings.remediation: Use a linear regex /^[0-9]+#$/ (no nested quantifier), bound input length, and validate on a worker or with a timeout.

findings.title: Weak password policy and username-enumerating login errors
findings.attack_path: Signup allows any 1-20 char password (strong-policy regex commented out) and login returns distinct 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' messages with no rate limiting or lockout. An attacker enumerates valid usernames then brute-forces weak passwords at scale.
findings.remediation: Enforce a strong password regex, return one generic auth error, and add rate limiting / lockout / CAPTCHA on /login.

findings.title: Verbose error handler leaks stack traces to clients
findings.attack_path: errorHandler renders the full err object (including stack) into error-template and returns it to the client. Triggering an error (e.g., malformed allocations/profile input) reveals file paths, library versions, and internal structure that aid further exploitation.
findings.remediation: Render a generic error page to users; log details server-side only; set NODE_ENV=production and strip stack traces from responses.

findings.title: Default/seeded predictable credentials including admin account
findings.attack_path: artifacts/db-reset.js seeds admin/Admin_123, user1/User1_123, user2/User2_123 as cleartext passwords. If the seed runs against a real deployment (the script supports NODE_ENV=production and Heroku postdeploy), an attacker logs straight into the admin account with the published default password.
findings.remediation: Never seed default accounts in non-dev environments; if seeding is needed, force a password reset on first login and hash all seeded credentials.

findings.title: Outdated / vulnerable dependencies and EOL base image
findings.attack_path: package.json pins old, knowingly-vulnerable libraries (marked 0.3.5, mongodb 2.x, swig 1.4.2, needle 2.2.4) and the Dockerfile uses node:12-alpine (EOL). A supply-chain or known-CVE exploit against any of these (e.g., marked XSS/ReDoS) reaches the app, and the unpatched runtime widens the blast radius.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to supported library versions and a supported Node LTS base image; add automated dependency/CVE scanning (npm audit, Dependabot) to CI.

findings.title: Log injection / forging via unsanitized username in login logging
findings.attack_path: On a failed login, session.js logs the raw userName ('attempt to login with invalid user: <userName>'). A username containing CRLF lets an attacker forge or split log lines, inject fake entries, and undermine the integrity of audit trails used for incident response.
findings.remediation: Encode/sanitize user input before logging (strip CRLF), use structured logging, and treat log fields as untrusted data.

findings.title: Container/runtime hardening and DB exposure gaps
findings.attack_path: The Dockerfile leaves the production privilege-drop/chmod hardening line commented out, and docker-compose runs MongoDB with no authentication on the shared network (mongodb://mongo:27017 with no credentials). A compromised web container (e.g., via TM-001/TM-002) reaches an unauthenticated database and can read/modify all collections, then attempt lateral movement.
findings.remediation: Enable the non-root hardening lines, require MongoDB auth + network policy, run least-privilege containers, and segment the data tier.

findings.title: Memos are global/shared across all users (broken access control on read)
findings.attack_path: MemosDAO.getAllMemos returns every memo with no userId filter and addMemos stores no owner. Any authenticated user reads memos written by any other user, leaking potentially sensitive internal notes, and this shared surface is also what makes the stored-XSS (TM-007) cross-user.
findings.remediation: Scope memo storage and retrieval to the owning userId; enforce per-record authorization on read and write.
